Timeline::sizes¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

auto Timeline::sizes() const

What It Tells You¶

sizes() returns the logical extent of every axis. A scalar has no axes and therefore reports []; a vector of two instants reports [2]; a two-row, two-column timeline reports [2, 2].

The returned object is a lightweight read-only range. Iterate it, index it, or construct an owning std::vector<std::int64_t> when the shape must outlive the timeline. Keeping the public example type as auto avoids coupling application code to the range implementation.

Shape describes arrangement, not chronology. [2, 2] says how positions are addressed; it does not claim the timestamps are sorted, unique, equally spaced, or in the same calendar period.

Returns¶

A read-only range of signed 64-bit extents in outermost-to-innermost order. Its length equals dim(), and the product of its extents equals numel().

Examples¶

Example 1. Read scalar, vector, and matrix shapes without exposing a concrete range type.

auto print_shape = [](const pluss::Timeline& value) {
    std::cout << '[';
    std::size_t i = 0;
    for (auto extent : value.sizes()) {
        if (i++ != 0) std::cout << ',';
        std::cout << extent;
    }
    std::cout << ']';
};

auto scalar = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:30:00Z");
auto vector = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-02-29T12:30:00Z", "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z"
});
auto matrix = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-02-29T12:30:00Z", "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z"},
    {"2024-03-02T06:15:00Z", ""},
});

print_shape(scalar); std::cout << "\n";
print_shape(vector); std::cout << "\n";
print_shape(matrix); std::cout << "\n";

Output¶

[]
[2]
[2,2]

Example 2. Take an owning copy when a separate shape value is required.

auto times = pluss::timeline::epoch({2, 3});
std::vector<std::int64_t> shape(times.sizes().begin(), times.sizes().end());

std::cout << "rank=" << shape.size()
          << ", rows=" << shape[0]
          << ", columns=" << shape[1] << "\n";

Output¶

rank=2, rows=2, columns=3

Example 3. Empty axes remain part of the shape.

auto empty = pluss::timeline::epoch({2, 0, 4});
std::cout << "dim=" << empty.dim() << ", numel=" << empty.numel() << "\n";

Output¶

dim=3, numel=0

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • A scalar shape is [], not [1]. The latter is a one-element vector.

  • An extent of zero does not remove an axis; [2, 0, 4] still has rank 3.

  • Timeline supports ranks 0 through 3; factories reject higher-rank shapes.

  • Treat the returned range as a borrowed view. Copy it before storing it beyond the lifetime of its timeline.
